title: Nodal runway buffer and tiered commit map
body:
Executive summary:
This sheet maps a node-based approach to runway buffering, headcount phasing, and tiered-commit pricing sensitivity. Purpose: produce a small actionable playbook (1) to protect 6+ month runway against token-price shocks, (2) to gate hires by revenue/price elasticity triggers, and (3) to define which commit tiers (retainer / slab / burst) to offer or retract by scenario.

Key definitions / nomenclature:
- Nodal buffer: discrete reserve buckets (Node A/B/C) representing operating levers: payroll cadence (A), reserved GPU seats (B), and credit/burst pool (C).
- Commit tiers: Retainer (monthly reserved capacity), Slab (90d prepaid capacity with discounts), Burst (on-demand credits at premium).
- Price tilt: a % change in per-token price to customers; we analyze elasticity around -20% to +30%.

Assumptions (base):
- Current committed monthly burn (CMB): $2.1M (salaries $1.2M, infra $650k, ops & S&M $250k).
- Average revenue per token (ARPT) baseline: $0.0006/token.
- Active paid customers: 430 (mix: 60% self-serve, 30% mid-market, 10% enterprise).
- GPU cost per reserved seat (effective amortized): $9,500/month.
- Average tokens per paid customer per month: 12M.
- Hiring lead time: 8 weeks for IC, 12 weeks for senior eng/infra.

Scenario overview (3 node scenarios):
- Conservative (Downside): 25% drop in ARPT and 10% customer churn over 4 months.
- Base: no change in ARPT, steady growth +6% customers/quarter.
- Aggressive (Upside): +15% ARPT (price increases or upsell) and +12% customers in 3 months.

Quick scenario table (monthly delta projections):
| Scenario      | Monthly Burn ($) | Headcount net delta (FTE) | Runway months (starting cash assumption) |
| Conservative  | 1,900,000        | -6                        | 4.7                                     |
| Base          | 2,100,000        | +3                        | 6.2                                     |
| Aggressive    | 2,350,000        | +8                        | 7.1                                     |

Headcount phasing (role-level nodal plan):
- Node A (payroll cadence short-term buffer): freeze non-critical IC hires when runway < 5m.
- Node A hires proposed Q1: 2 infra engs (S), 1 ML infra IC, 1 finance associate (rev ops).
- Node B (reserved capacity ops) staffing: maintain 1 dedicated on-call ops engineer per 40 reserved seats; reduce contractor pool if slab utilization < 50%.

Role table (planned hires vs gate triggers):
| Role                 | Planned Q1 hires | Cost/month (fully loaded) | Gate trigger (when to pause)                |
| Sr Infra Eng         | 2                | $33,000                   | Runway < 5 months OR slab-utilization < 60%  |
| ML Infra IC          | 1                | $15,000                   | ARPT drop > 15% sustained 6 weeks           |
| Finance Associate    | 1                | $7,000                    | N/A (critical for commit restructuring)     |
| Customer Success IC  | 2                | $12,000                   | If enterprise net-new MRR < $120k / quarter |

Pricing sensitivity model (method):
- We compute revenue change for a ±5/10/20/30% price movement assuming elasticities: self-serve elasticity e=1.8, mid-market e=0.7, enterprise e=0.3. Elasticity describes % change in volume for 1% price change.
- Revenue change = sum over segments of ARPT * tokens * (1 + pct_price_change) * (1 + elasticity * pct_price_change).

Example outputs (monthly revenue delta from baseline $1.55M):
- Price -20%:
  - Self-serve: revenue change ≈ -32% (high elasticity)
  - Mid-market: ≈ -14%
  - Enterprise: ≈ -6%
  - Total revenue ≈ -23% (~$1.19M) -> Burn gap = +$910k/month vs base, requiring draw from Node C or cut hires.
- Price +15%:
  - Self-serve: revenue change ≈ -27% (volume loss) but higher ARPT partially offsets -> net segment change ≈ -13%
  - Mid-market: +9%
  - Enterprise: +4%
  - Total revenue ≈ +4% (~$1.61M) -> Can fund 1–2 hiring slots or expand slab discounts.

Break-even analysis for slab discounting: when offering a slab discount d% (upfront 90d), we need uplift U in uptake or retention such that: (ARPT*(1-d))*tokens*U >= ARPT*tokens (baseline over 90 days). Rearranged: U >= 1/(1-d). For d=20%, U >= 1.25 (25% uplift).
Practical: 20% slab discount only advisable if historical slab uplift > 30% or it reduces churn materially.

Nodal buffer playbook (operational triggers):
1) Runway monitor (daily): Runway < 5.5 months -> tag Node A: pause non-critical IC hiring, delay discretionary cloud projects.
2) Price shock detection: 2 consecutive weeks of ARPT decline > 12% -> Node C engage: pull $500k from burst credit line and prioritize enterprise upsell campaigns.
3) Slab utilization check: slab utilization < 55% and churn > 8% in same month -> reduce slab capacity by 20% next quarter and reallocate budget to marketing for mid-market.
4) Hiring fallback: Senior offers that would increase fixed burn > $50k/month require CFO + VP Eng approval when runway < 6 months.

Sensitivity matrix (decision thresholds):
- If ARPT falls -15% and churn +6% -> enact conservative scenario: cut contractor hours (Node A), postpone slab expansion (Node B), engage PR/partnership to shore enterprise deals (Node C).
- If ARPT increases +10% -> invest 40% of additional margin into RU (reserved units) and 60% into headcount accretive hires (infra & SRE).

Recommended immediate actions (next 30 days):
- Approve finance associate hire (critical for near-term commit-tier repricing) but mark as conditional (start date deferred by 4 weeks if slab-util < 60%).
- Lock a $750k short-term burst credit facility (Node C) at 1.8% monthly interest - cheaper than hiring freeze productivity loss in modeled downside.
- Run a 2-week price experiment for mid-market: +8% ARPT with controlled messaging and measure net MRR delta; if +6% uplift within 14 days, consider permanent +5% repositioning for mid-market.

Notes & open questions:
- Need better slab-utilization telemetry by region; current sheet aggregates globally which masks APAC vs NA differences.
- Confirm amortization assumptions for on-prem customer passthroughs (we currently assume uniform GPU seat cost).
- Ask Product: can we create a restricted slab product (no burst) that would reduce churn among low-util mid-market customers?

Appendix: quick formula cheatsheet (text):
- Runway = Cash / MonthlyBurn.
- Effective revenue after price move = ARPT*(1+Δp)*(1 + elasticity*Δp)*tokens*customers.
- Required uplift for slab discount d: U_required = 1/(1-d).

Author notes: this is intended as a working sheet with toggles to be moved into a live gsheet (linked artifact). The next iteration should attach a small Monte Carlo (1000 draws) sampling customer churn and ARPT shock distributions to produce probabilistic runway buckets.

Prepared by: Aisha Banerjee (finance). Last reviewed: 2026-02-03.
summary: Node-based budget and headcount plan linking tiered-commit pricing sensitivity to concrete hiring gates and runbook triggers. Focus: protect runway while enabling targeted hires when price/mix improves.
